risk_if_not_implemented: Without Transmission Medium Security, security, compliance and resilience activities may lack direction, ownership and executive support, leaving required controls unperformed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), Loss of Data / Service Availability (R-IP-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to natural threats NT-2, NT-3, NT-4, NT-5, NT-6, NT-8, NT-10, NT-11, NT-12, NT-13, NT-14; Physical Crime (MT-5), Human Error (MT-9), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14).

compensating_control_1.name: Supporting Utilities
compensating_control_1.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to protect power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction.
compensating_control_1.justification: Supporting Utilities (PES-20) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Transmission Medium Security (PES-16.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Facility applicability. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Physical Access Control
compensating_control_2.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to enforce physical access authorizations for all physical access points (including designated entry/exit points) to facilities (excluding those areas within the facility officially designated as publicly accessible).
compensating_control_2.justification: Physical Access Control (PES-08) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Transmission Medium Security (PES-16.1) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
